title: Error boundaries and recovery

sources.locator: React Learn and Reference; React 19.2; provisions applicable to Error boundaries and recovery
sources.claim: React error boundaries catch render-tree errors below them and show recovery UI, while async, event, and server errors need their own handling.

canonicalExplanation.summary: If a component throws **while rendering**, React unmounts the whole tree and the learner sees a blank page, unless an **error boundary** above it catches the error and shows a fallback instead. Place boundaries around routes or features so one broken widget doesn't take down the app. A good fallback says something human, offers **Try again** (which resets the boundary) and shows a short incident id, never a stack trace. Boundaries only catch errors thrown during rendering; **event-handler errors and rejected fetches** aren't caught, so handle those with try/catch and error state.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A lesson page renders a code-runner widget. When a lesson's example data is malformed, the widget throws during render and the entire app goes white: no navigation, no way back. A route boundary reports a safe incident id and lets the learner retry without exposing stack details. In this lesson you'll design and test a route or feature error boundary with useful fallback and reset behavior.

```predict
{"question": "A button's onClick throws. Does the nearest error boundary show its fallback?", "options": ["Yes", "No: boundaries catch render errors, not event-handler errors"], "answer": 1, "why": "Wrap handler code in try/catch and set error state; the boundary won't see it."}
```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know the **Routing and application context** module, the **Remote data and asynchronous UI** module, **Loading, empty, success and failure states**, and **Errors, throw and recovery boundaries** (throw, catch and safe messages).

sections.heading: The model: a boundary per route or feature
Where to place boundaries

includes: Wrap routes or features in error boundaries with human fallbacks, retry and incident ids.
Handle event and async errors separately, and test the fallback and reset.
excludes: Writing class-based boundaries from scratch in depth.

outcomes: Design and test a route or feature error boundary with useful fallback and reset behavior.

examples.title: A lesson page that fails gracefully
examples.situation: A route boundary reports a safe incident id and lets the learner retry without exposing stack details.
walkthrough: **Contain:** the lesson route is wrapped in an ErrorBoundary, so the header and navigation stay usable.
**Report a safe incident id:** the fallback logs the message with a short id and shows only the id and a friendly sentence.
**Retry:** a test will make LessonPage throw once, check the alert text, click Try again, and see the lesson render.
examples.result: A broken lesson shows a calm message with a reference and a retry, while the rest of the app keeps working.

examples.title: The save error nobody saw
examples.situation: A Save button's handler throws when the server returns bad JSON. The team expected the error boundary to show a message, but nothing appears.
walkthrough: Errors in event handlers don't reach error boundaries.
Wrap the handler's await in try/catch.
Set an error state and render a role="alert" message next to the button.
examples.result: Learners see "Couldn't save. Try again." when the save fails.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: One error boundary catches rejected fetches and every event-handler exception automatically.
misconceptions.correction: Error boundaries only catch errors thrown while React is rendering their children. Event handlers and async work need their own try/catch and error state.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "The save error nobody saw", why didn't the boundary react?

analogy.example: Error boundaries are like **fuses in a house**. A fault in one room's wiring (a component) trips that room's fuse, and the rest of the house stays lit. But a fuse doesn't notice a dropped plate (an event-handler error); someone in the room has to deal with that.
usefulFor: reset = flipping the fuse back on
limitations: Fuses don't show messages; fallbacks should.
One fuse for the whole house means everything goes dark.

nearTransfer.prompt: Wrap a comments widget in its own ErrorBoundary with a small fallback ("Comments are unavailable") and a Try again button, leaving the lesson content visible.
expectedEvidence: Lesson stays visible when comments fail.

farTransfer.prompt: Add route-level and widget-level boundaries to an app, plus try/catch error states for two event handlers. Write tests that force each kind of error and check what the learner sees.
scaffold: A test component that throws on demand.
expectedEvidence: Handler errors shown as inline messages.

remediation.explanation: For each possible failure ask: **Is it thrown while rendering?** Then a boundary. **In a handler or promise?** Then try/catch and error state. For each boundary ask: **what stays usable, and how does the learner retry?**
remediation.retryPrompt: Apply this to "The save error nobody saw".

recap.summary: To design and test a route or feature error boundary, wrap routes and risky widgets so render errors stay local, show a friendly fallback with a safe incident id and a Try again that resets, send details to logs, and handle event-handler and async errors separately with try/catch and error state.
